title: The culture of giving cards
paragraphs: The tradition of sending greeting cards has withstood the rise of digital communication. Though often inexpensive, cards can convey our thoughts and emotions. Their rich history spreads over centuries of civilisations across the world, building a culture of card giving along its way.

It was written in a 2011 edition of Souvenirs, Gifts, & Novelties that since the earliest days of written interaction, special occasions such as birthdays and seasonal celebrations have been recognised through handwritten notes and letters. Ancient Egyptians wrote scrolls. In China, wishes of good fortune were sent in decorative red envelopes around Chinese New Year. And similarly, cards featuring classical Persian poetic verse written in calligraphy were exchanged. These gestures paved the way for the culture of greeting cards.

Before the printing revolution of the 15th century, only those with lots of money would write cards. Since then, they have become more accessible, meaning more people could communicate from a distance. As industrialisation continued to sweep through the 19th century, sending cards became a widespread practice.

During the Victorian period, greeting cards became quite elaborate in design. They were adorned with lace, ribbon, and intricate illustrations. The cards themselves became keepsakes, treasured for their beauty and sentiment. Nowadays, we see a variety of designs. Most cards still leave a blank space inside for a handwritten message. Some cards can even be designed online to include pictures of loved ones, adding a more personal touch.

According to Ken Research, from 2024 the global greeting card market was valued at around $19 billion. With that, and increasing concerns about the environment, many manufacturers are changing how they make their cards. They're using recycled and other environmentally friendly materials, like biodegradable glitter and paper made from sustainable plant fibres like bamboo. So, we can continue our kind tradition of card giving without harming the planet.
chineseParagraphs: 寄送贺卡的传统经受住了数字通信兴起的考验。尽管贺卡通常价格低廉，但它们能传达我们的思想和情感。其丰富的历史跨越了世界各地的数个世纪文明，在此过程中建立了赠送贺卡的文化。
2011年版的《纪念品、礼品与新奇事物》中提到，从书面交流的最早期开始，生日和季节性庆祝等特殊场合就通过手写便条和信件来认可。古埃及人书写卷轴。在中国，农历新年期间，人们会用装饰性的红色信封寄送恭喜发财的祝福。同样，印有用精美书法书写的古典波斯诗句的贺卡也会被交换。这些举动为贺卡文化铺平了道路。
在15世纪印刷革命之前，只有富人才能写贺卡。此后，贺卡变得更普及，意味着更多人可以进行远距离交流。随着工业化在19世纪继续蔓延，寄送贺卡成为一种普遍的做法。
在维多利亚时代，贺卡的设计变得相当精美。它们装饰有蕾丝、缎带和复杂的插图。贺卡本身成为纪念品，因其美丽和情感寓意而备受珍视。如今，我们看到各种各样的设计。大多数贺卡内部仍留有空白空间用于手写信息。有些贺卡甚至可以在线设计，包含亲人的照片，增添更多个人特色。
根据Ken Research的数据，从2024年起，全球贺卡市场估值约为190亿美元。鉴于这一点，以及日益增长的环保担忧，许多制造商正在改变他们制作贺卡的方式。他们使用再生纸和其他环保材料，如可生物降解的闪光粉和由竹子等可持续植物纤维制成的纸张。这样，我们就可以在不损害地球的情况下，继续我们赠送贺卡的友善传统。

vocabulary.entry: withstand /wɪðˈstænd/ v. 经受住，承受（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The building withstood the earthquake.
vocabulary.translation: 这座建筑经受住了地震。

vocabulary.entry: convey /kənˈveɪ/ v. 传达，表达（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The music conveys a sense of sadness.
vocabulary.translation: 这段音乐传达出一种悲伤的感觉。

vocabulary.entry: edition /ɪˈdɪʃn/ n. 版本，版次
vocabulary.example: The second edition of the book was published in 2020.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书的第二版于2020年出版。

vocabulary.entry: scroll /skrəʊl/ n. 卷轴
vocabulary.example: Ancient texts were often written on scrolls.
vocabulary.translation: 古代文献通常写在卷轴上。

vocabulary.entry: decorative /ˈdekərətɪv/ adj. 装饰性的，用于装饰的
vocabulary.example: The room was filled with decorative items.
vocabulary.translation: 房间里摆满了装饰品。

vocabulary.entry: red envelope /ˌred ˈenvələʊp/ n. 红包（中式传统）
vocabulary.example: Red envelopes are given during Chinese New Year.
vocabulary.translation: 红包在春节期间赠送。

vocabulary.entry: classical /ˈklæsɪkl/ adj. 经典的，古典的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She is studying classical literature.
vocabulary.translation: 她在研究古典文学。

vocabulary.definition: 波斯的，波斯人的（专有名词）
vocabulary.entry: Persian /ˈpɜːʒn/ adj. 波斯的，波斯人的（专有名词）
vocabulary.example: Persian poetry is known for its beauty.
vocabulary.translation: 波斯诗歌以其优美著称。

vocabulary.entry: poetic verse /pəʊˈetɪk vɜːs/ n. 诗句，诗体（书面语）
vocabulary.example: He wrote poetic verse in his diary.
vocabulary.translation: 他在日记里写诗。

vocabulary.entry: calligraphy /kəˈlɪɡrəfi/ n. 书法（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She is learning Chinese calligraphy.
vocabulary.translation: 她在学习中国书法。

vocabulary.entry: gesture /ˈdʒestʃə(r)/ n. 姿态，举动（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The donation was a generous gesture.
vocabulary.translation: 这笔捐款是一个慷慨的举动。

vocabulary.entry: pave the way for /ˌpeɪv ðə ˈweɪ fɔː(r)/ phr. 为……铺平道路（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: His research paved the way for later discoveries.
vocabulary.translation: 他的研究为后来的发现铺平了道路。

vocabulary.entry: printing revolution /ˈprɪntɪŋ ˌrevəˈluːʃn/ n. 印刷革命（历史术语）
vocabulary.example: The printing revolution made books more accessible.
vocabulary.translation: 印刷革命使书籍更普及。

vocabulary.definition: 可获得的，易接近的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: accessible /əkˈsesəbl/ adj. 可获得的，易接近的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The website is accessible to all users.
vocabulary.translation: 所有用户都可以访问该网站。

vocabulary.entry: industrialisation /ɪnˌdʌstriəlaɪˈzeɪʃn/ n. 工业化（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The industrialisation of the 19th century changed society.
vocabulary.translation: 19世纪的工业化改变了社会。

vocabulary.entry: widespread /ˈwaɪdspred/ adj. 广泛的，普遍的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The disease is now widespread in the region.
vocabulary.translation: 这种疾病现在在该地区广泛传播。

vocabulary.entry: elaborate /ɪˈlæbərət/ adj. 精巧的，复杂的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The wedding was an elaborate affair.
vocabulary.translation: 这场婚礼办得很隆重。

vocabulary.entry: adorn /əˈdɔːn/ v. 装饰，点缀（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The room was adorned with beautiful flowers.
vocabulary.translation: 房间里装饰着美丽的花。

vocabulary.entry: lace /leɪs/ n. 蕾丝，花边
vocabulary.example: The dress was trimmed with lace.
vocabulary.translation: 这条裙子饰有蕾丝花边。

vocabulary.entry: ribbon /ˈrɪbən/ n. 丝带，缎带
vocabulary.example: She tied a red ribbon around the gift.
vocabulary.translation: 她在礼物上系了一条红丝带。

vocabulary.entry: intricate /ˈɪntrɪkət/ adj. 复杂精细的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The watch mechanism is extremely intricate.
vocabulary.translation: 这块手表的机芯极其复杂精细。

vocabulary.entry: illustration /ˌɪləˈstreɪʃn/ n. 插图，说明图
vocabulary.example: The book is full of beautiful illustrations.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书里满是精美的插图。

vocabulary.entry: keepsake /ˈkiːpseɪk/ n. 纪念品，信物（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She kept the ring as a keepsake.
vocabulary.translation: 她保留了这枚戒指作为纪念品。

vocabulary.entry: treasured /ˈtreʒəd/ adj. 珍爱的，珍贵的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Her most treasured possession is her grandmother's watch.
vocabulary.translation: 她最珍爱的物品是她祖母的手表。

vocabulary.entry: sentiment /ˈsentɪmənt/ n. 情感，情绪（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The card expressed her true sentiments.
vocabulary.translation: 这张贺卡表达了她真实的情感。

vocabulary.entry: personal touch /ˈpɜːsənl tʌtʃ/ n. 个人特色（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Adding a handwritten note gives a personal touch.
vocabulary.translation: 添加手写便条增添了个性化色彩。

vocabulary.entry: manufacturer /ˌmænjuˈfæktʃərə(r)/ n. 制造商，生产商
vocabulary.example: The car manufacturer has recalled thousands of vehicles.
vocabulary.translation: 这家汽车制造商召回了数千辆汽车。

vocabulary.definition: 可生物降解的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: biodegradable /ˌbaɪəʊdɪˈɡreɪdəbl/ adj. 可生物降解的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: These bags are made from biodegradable materials.
vocabulary.translation: 这些袋子是由可生物降解材料制成的。

vocabulary.entry: sustainable /səˈsteɪnəbl/ adj. 可持续的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The company is committed to sustainable development.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司致力于可持续发展。

vocabulary.entry: plant fibre /ˈplɑːnt faɪbə(r)/ n. 植物纤维（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Bamboo is a sustainable source of plant fibre.
vocabulary.translation: 竹子是可持续的植物纤维来源。

vocabulary.entry: bamboo /ˌbæmˈbuː/ n. 竹子
vocabulary.example: The panda eats bamboo shoots.
vocabulary.translation: 熊猫吃竹笋。
